boundary_decisions.rationale: The term names a compositional architecture and does not itself have one user, lifecycle, authority, SLO or semantic owner.
The suite packages replaceable products but cannot own imported table, catalog, query, policy or business semantics.
A coherent user and operating experience exists, but independent exit and cross-provider conformance evidence remain incomplete.
Table identity and state are semantic contracts realized by standards, libraries and capabilities; they become a product only when wrapped in an independent operated promise.
Catalog services have independent adopters, protocols, authority, lifecycle, failure and exit boundaries across multiple engines.
Query engines are independently adopted, operated, metered and replaceable while table and catalog state remain external.
Managed ingestion has its own users, source/delivery state, operation, economics and independently selectable table targets.
Maintenance algorithms remain capabilities/libraries, while a separately adopted service with destructive authority, SLO, support and exit is a product.
Sharing has independent providers/consumers, disclosure authority, protocol, availability, egress economics and revocation lifecycle.
Desired-state reconciliation is required, but present evidence does not prove a separate user adoption and exit boundary from the managed experience.
The suite consumes these contracts but must not re-own data fitness, derivation, purpose authority or business metrics.
Lakehouse is horizontal architecture. A solution pack must add an industry vocabulary, rules, source mappings, defaults and analytical recipes without changing horizontal semantics.

negative_tests.input_claim: Anything called a lakehouse is one product.
Apache Iceberg, Delta or Hudi table semantics are automatically products.
The lakehouse suite owns every meaning of its packaged products.
Observed implementation behavior overrides the published semantic contract.
An object-store path uniquely and sufficiently identifies an analytical table.
A catalog may redefine proposed table semantics while publishing a metadata pointer.
A successful physical query result is automatically an authoritative business fact.
A compaction or clustering job may change admitted logical results to improve performance.
Unreferenced-looking files may be deleted without retention, active-reader and legal-hold evidence.
XTable translation proves all Delta, Hudi and Iceberg features are semantically equivalent.
Durable object storage makes table commits serializable.
Every desired-state reconciler is automatically an independently adopted product.
Lakehouse supplies sports, banking, healthcare or oil-domain vocabulary and rules.
Adding an agent or model to a lakehouse capability creates a new lakehouse product or semantic owner.

ownership.invariant: Environment identity is distinct from every bound component identity.
Readiness is evaluated against an exact supported-component profile and evidence cut.
Table identity includes exact format edition and cannot be inferred from a path or catalog name alone.
A snapshot denotes one exact admitted table state; format translations preserve or explicitly refuse/loss-mark it.
A commit is valid only against its declared base state and edition-specific validation set.
Namespace identity is catalog-scoped and never equals table identity or business domain identity.
Publishing a current reference requires delegated authority and successful table commit preconditions.
Approval to publish a pointer is not authority to redefine the proposed table state.
A plan is bound to exact input cuts, connector capabilities, decisions and resource assumptions.
A result identifies its plan, input cuts and execution evidence but is not automatically a business fact.
A run is distinct from pipeline definition, attempt, source cut and table commit.
A receipt reports admitted and refused effects for an exact source/output cut.
Every destructive or rewriting action declares target cut, authority, retention, concurrency and finite budget.
Physical rewrite completion requires an executable equivalence oracle over admitted logical results.
A shared cut identifies source edition, snapshot/version and disclosure interval without transferring source ownership.
Sharing execution requires a purpose- and authority-scoped grant that remains independently revocable.
Every translation records unsupported features, residuals and information loss; silence is invalid.
Durability and consistency are properties of an exact provider offer, not consequences of table-format correctness.
Fitness is for a declared purpose and cut; successful table commit is not a quality certificate.
Observed runtime lineage is retained separately from causal or business-semantic claims.
Metric identity and formula remain portable across physical query engines and table formats.

scope: Provider-neutral lakehouse architecture, product, capability, semantic-contract, standard, library, implementation, provider-resource and neighboring-product boundaries.

sources.claim: Lakehouse is presented as an architectural pattern based on open direct-access formats, advanced analytics support and competitive data-management performance.
sources.scope_limit: The paper proposes and evaluates an architecture; it does not establish that lakehouse is one indivisible product or semantic owner.
sources.title: Lakehouse: A New Generation of Open Platforms that Unify Data Warehousing and Advanced Analytics

sources.claim: The specification defines table identity, immutable data and metadata files, snapshots, manifests, evolution and optimistic atomic metadata replacement.
sources.scope_limit: An interoperability specification is not an operated product, catalog service, object store or query engine.
sources.title: Apache Iceberg Table Specification

sources.claim: A common REST catalog API separates catalog interactions from languages and engines and supports change-based commits and credential vending.
sources.scope_limit: The protocol does not define every enterprise governance, discovery, storage or query semantic.
sources.title: Apache Iceberg REST Catalog Specification

sources.claim: The protocol defines serial table versions, atomic log actions, reader and writer requirements, protocol evolution and table features.
sources.scope_limit: Delta-specific identities and feature laws cannot be silently equated with Iceberg or Hudi semantics.
sources.title: Delta Transaction Log Protocol

sources.claim: The specification combines storage-format, reader/writer, timeline, MVCC and asynchronous table-service semantics.
sources.scope_limit: Hudi table services are capabilities of the table system unless wrapped in an independently adopted and operated service promise.
sources.title: Apache Hudi Technical Specification

sources.claim: Clustering has separate scheduling and execution phases, rewrites physical layout and records a replace action while preserving snapshot isolation constraints.
sources.scope_limit: The documentation establishes maintenance semantics, not a universal product boundary.
sources.title: Apache Hudi Clustering

sources.claim: XTable translates metadata among Delta, Hudi and Iceberg without defining a new table format.
sources.scope_limit: Translation is an interoperability capability; it neither proves semantic equivalence nor creates a table product.
sources.title: Apache XTable Overview

sources.claim: Cross-format translation has explicit feature and representation limitations, including unsupported generated columns and log/delete-vector behavior.
sources.scope_limit: Successful translation of a subset cannot justify lossless equivalence for every table feature.
sources.title: Apache XTable Features and Limitations

sources.claim: Polaris is an independently deployable Iceberg REST catalog interoperating with multiple engines.
sources.scope_limit: One implementation does not define the complete catalog semantic contract or qualify all provider offers.
sources.title: Apache Polaris

sources.claim: A query engine can independently bind an Iceberg table profile, one of several catalog types and one supported filesystem provider.
sources.scope_limit: Connector support is edition- and feature-bounded and includes potentially lossy type mappings.
sources.title: Trino Iceberg Connector

sources.claim: A specialist provider sells managed ingestion independently across Hudi, Iceberg and Delta table targets.
sources.scope_limit: Vendor claims establish market/adoption evidence, not universal semantics, performance truth or qualification.
sources.title: OneFlow Data Ingestion

sources.claim: A specialist provider offers table compaction, clustering and cleaning as a separately operated managed service with support posture.
sources.scope_limit: The product currently emphasizes Hudi and cannot establish format-neutral conformance by claim alone.
sources.title: Onehouse Table Optimizer

sources.claim: A specialist analytics provider packages an Iceberg REST catalog as a separately described product surface with governance and maintenance capabilities.
sources.scope_limit: Bundled features do not transfer semantic ownership from table, policy, lineage or maintenance contexts.
sources.title: Dremio Open Catalog

sources.claim: A specialist provider offers a distributed analytical query engine that binds open tables and catalogs independently.
sources.scope_limit: Marketing performance claims require independent benchmarks and exact workload/edition qualification.
sources.title: Dremio Intelligent Query Engine

sources.claim: An open protocol separates governed dataset exchange from the computing platform used by provider and consumer.
sources.scope_limit: The protocol does not supply enterprise purpose authority, business meaning or complete disclosure governance.
sources.title: Delta Sharing

sources.claim: A platform is managed as a product around user outcomes while curating replaceable capabilities behind consistent interfaces.
sources.scope_limit: General platform guidance does not ratify any lakehouse product or define data semantics.
sources.title: CNCF Platforms White Paper
